$comment: THE CROSS-REPO CONTRACT. Every invariant that spans capucor-web, capucor-os and
capucor-docs, in one machine-readable place instead of prose in two AGENTS.md files.
WHY IT EXISTS. The 2026-08-04 audit kept finding the same four classes of drift —
coupled dependencies, the provisioning/schema contract, backup coverage, and files
duplicated on purpose — and every single one was caught by a person noticing, not by
anything failing. Drift that only a careful reader catches is drift that ships.
HOW IT IS ENFORCED. `capucor-os/scripts/audit-cross-repo.mjs` (npm run audit) reads
this file and checks every class against all three repos. It is READ-ONLY: it changes
nothing, writes nothing, and touches no production state.
WHY THREE COPIES. capucor-docs holds the canonical copy; capucor-web and capucor-os
each carry a byte-identical vendored copy under contracts/. A CI job runs in ONE
repo's checkout and cannot see its siblings, so a vendored copy is the only way the
in-repo test (src/__tests__/cross-repo-contract.test.ts) can enforce anything from
here. The cross-repo audit compares the three copies to each other, so a drifted copy
is caught by the same command it belongs to. Edit the capucor-docs copy first.

coupledDependencies.why: Next, OpenNext and Wrangler are a runtime TRIPLE, not three independent packages: OpenNext 1.20.x requires Next >=16.2.11, and moving one side alone can make a clean install select an adapter whose Next peer range the app does not satisfy. React and supabase-js are shared because both Workers render the same components and speak to the same PostgREST. All are pinned EXACT (no caret) on purpose — PH-01 pinned them after an unverified runtime pair shipped.

node.why: The dev box runs Node 24 / npm 11. CI ran Node 20 until 2026-08-03 and a lockfile written by npm 11 was rejected outright by npm 10. `.nvmrc` and the `setup-node` step in ci.yml must move together or that trap returns.

provisioning.why: A client signs on capucor.com and capucor-web starts a write whose schema lives in capucor-os. A rename on either side produces NO compile error and NO failing test in either repo. The symptom is a paying client whose durable portal stage keeps retrying.
provisioning.blindSpot: Since migration 017 an `after insert` trigger (client_orgs_default_entity -> ensure_default_entity) runs INSIDE the provisioning insert. Both tripwires are blind to it — one drives an in-memory fake, the other checks table invariants. If it ever raises, the insert aborts and a paying client gets no portal access. Verify it live, per PO-01's seam test.

handSynced.why: These files exist in both app repos and a one-sided edit costs money or breaks a seam, with no compile error and no failing test. The per-repo digests below are what lets a SINGLE repo's CI notice a one-sided edit: change the file, the digest moves, that repo goes red naming its counterpart. Regenerate the values with `npm run audit -- --print-digests` in capucor-os and paste them into all three copies of this file.

pairModes.byte: The two copies must be identical after whitespace normalisation.
pairModes.code: The two copies must be identical after comments and blank lines are stripped. Each repo keeps its own explanatory banner — they all carry one, and they should.
pairModes.independent: The two copies legitimately differ. No cross-repo equality is asserted; the digests still pin each side so a one-sided edit is visible. `expectedCodeDiffLines` bounds how far apart they are allowed to drift.

files.why: Both repos price the same proposals off the same `brackets` table — capucor.com when a lead builds one, capucor.app when staff amend one. Drift means two different quotes for one selection.

Same pricing math, but capucor-os routes the bracket-fetch failure through its own `lib/log.ts` while capucor-web still uses console.error. That is the ONLY sanctioned divergence: three lines (one import, one call site each). If the count moves, the math itself may have drifted.

PRICING_ADDONS is the server-side WHITELIST of accepted add-on slugs and their prices, not display strings. Reprice an add-on in one repo only and the two apps quote different totals, or one silently drops an add-on the other charges for.

Both repos mint into the SAME unique client_orgs.slug column from two different Workers. A divergence in the slugify rule or the collision suffix surfaces as a unique-constraint violation on a paying client's first insert.

The retry runner in capucor-os rebuilds a capucor-web message from this file and sends it under the ORIGINAL idempotency key. A divergence means the retry sends different content from the original, inside Resend's 24-hour idempotency window.

knownDuplicates.why: Same-path files that are identical in both repos but are not worth the friction of a pinned digest — design primitives, thin client factories, and generated types. The audit still enforces the declared relationship across repos. Its real job is the INVERSE check: an identical same-path file that appears in neither this list nor handSynced is reported, so a new accidental duplicate has to be classified rather than quietly accumulate.

entries.why: shadcn/Base-Nova primitives. Drift is a visual inconsistency between the marketing site and the OS, not a data bug — but the two surfaces are meant to look like one product.
The service-role and cookieless client factories. Both repos read the same tables under the same policies; a divergence here is a silent-zero-rows bug.
One-time link tokens minted by capucor-web and consumed by flows both repos touch.
cn() plus firstOfNextMonth(), which decides the first debit date shown on a proposal and written into a subscription period.
The per-IP token bucket. Namespacing rules differ per repo but the bucket implementation must not.
On Cloudflare the real client IP is CF-Connecting-IP; x-forwarded-for is the worker loopback and collapses every visitor into one bucket. Both repos rate-limit and both record signer IPs.
The PH-08b body cap. Per-route limits differ; the content-length-then-running-count helper must not.
The HMAC that gates detailed /api/health. Both CI workflows sign with the same scheme; a divergence silently drops one repo back to the public view.
Generated from ONE Supabase project by `npm run db:types`. If the two copies differ, one repo regenerated after a migration and the other did not — which is the only way this file can drift at all.

Toolchain configuration. Both Workers are built by the same pinned Next/OpenNext pair, so a divergence here means one repo is being linted, styled or bundled differently from the thing it is supposed to be identical to.

The same incremental-cache override in both, but the COMMENTS deliberately differ: capucor-web's describes real ISR on / and /pricing, while capucor-os's records that the same comment was copied over in Phase 1a and was false there — no /api/revalidate, and `revalidate` is banned on every per-user route. Each Worker must keep its OWN KV namespace regardless; both apps have a "/" route key, so a shared one makes one app serve the other's cached page.
Shared URLs and senders, but each repo declares its own origin defaults.
Phase 3 dropped the OS-only types (SubscriptionSummary, SubscriptionStatus, ProposalRow) from capucor-web's copy. Only the pricing shapes are shared — this is no longer a straight mirror.

syncedTriples.why: Files that must be identical in all three repos. Checked repo-to-repo by the cross-repo audit only; a digest recorded inside a file cannot cover that file itself.

routeSeam.why: One Worker per domain, split by host-based redirects, with each repo holding one half of the table. A path dropped from the wrong list turns an old bookmark or an already-sent email link into a 404.

os.note: /proposal/:path* is the one that looks removable and is not: the signing document lives on capucor.com, but proposal links in already-sent emails were minted against capucor.app.

routeSeam.forbiddenWhy: A 301 on a POST downgrades it to GET and drops the body. Redirecting /_next or /brand off capucor.app strips the CSS and logo from every portal page — which is why the lists are explicit rather than a negative-lookahead catch-all.

backup.why: The dump is the only copy of the signed debit-order mandates. Supabase Free includes no platform backups and no PITR.
keyPrefixDeclaredIn: Cloudflare R2 lifecycle rule — 185-day expiry (dashboard only, NOT checkable from here)
Cloudflare R2 bucket-lock rule — 180-day retention (dashboard only, NOT checkable from here)
backup.keyPrefixWarning: One fact in three places and only the code half is testable. Changing KEY_PREFIX without changing both Cloudflare rules silently un-retains and un-expires every object.
backup.zeroDependencyWhy: These jobs are checkout + setup-node + `node script.mjs` BY DESIGN. No `npm ci`, which is the difference between a run billing one minute against the free 2,000 and billing five. Do not add one.
backup.weakestLink: GitHub disables scheduled workflows after 60 days of repository inactivity, which stops the job and with it BOTH destinations. There is no alert.

migrationLedger.evidence: 2026-08-05, read-only query against the linked project: `select count(*) from information_schema.schemata where schema_name = 'supabase_migrations'` returned 0. The ledger SCHEMA does not exist, so the ledger holds nothing at all — not 001-017 and not 018-022. This is a stronger statement than the earlier prose ('does not contain 001-017'), which assumed the table existed and was partially filled.
migrationLedger.pushForbiddenWhy: A 2026-08-04 `supabase db push` dry run proposed replaying every plain `create table` migration from 001 against a live database that already has all 27 tables. Until the repair plan is reviewed, apply the one intended file with `supabase db query --linked --file` and let `npm run db:check` prove the result.
migrationLedger.filenamePatternWhy: The Supabase CLI parses a migration version as the leading digits up to the first underscore. A suffixed name is not skipped with a warning — it is not seen as a migration at all.
migrationLedger.knownNonConformingWhy: There were two 009_ files until 2026-08-03. They were suffixed rather than renumbered so the file order still reflects when they were actually applied. Renaming them is part of the repair plan, not a tidy-up to do casually.

fixedPaths.why: Two SessionStart hooks in .claude/hooks/ read these files by hard-coded path and grep for a control line. Moving or renaming either breaks the nudge SILENTLY — the hook exits 0 on a missing file by design, so nothing ever reports it.

docs.why: The board, the tracker and the two AGENTS.md files are load-bearing navigation. A relative link that stopped resolving is the cheapest possible drift to catch and the easiest to leave rotting.
docs.linkCheckExcludeWhy: archive/ is frozen history. Its documents cite files at the paths they had when the work was done, and a good number of those files were deleted in Phase 3 of the OS split. Rewriting those links to today's paths would make the record say something that was never true, and deleting them would lose the citation. A link checker that forces a historical document to describe the present is a checker that gets switched off.
